relations.myth: Kamsa’s plots against the prophesied child
relations.note: Kamsa repeatedly engineers Kṛṣṇa’s death before confronting him in the arena.

relations.myth: Death of Kamsa in the arena
relations.note: Kṛṣṇa seizes Kamsa, throws him from the platform, and kills him.
Kamsa is Kṛṣṇa’s maternal uncle in the dominant narrative tradition.
Kamsa plots Balarāma’s death; Balarāma helps destroy his champions and faction.
Balarāma is Kamsa’s other nephew and opponent in epic-Purāṇic tradition.

relations.myth: Viṣṇu kills Kamsa’s previous incarnation Kālanemi
relations.note: Viṣṇu kills Kālanemi, who is subsequently reborn as Kamsa.
The Purāṇa identifies Kamsa as the asura Kālanemi reborn.

relations.myth: Kamsa attacks the exchanged infant goddess
relations.note: Kamsa tries to smash her against stone; she escapes and prophesies his killer.

relations.myth: Nārada reveals the concealed brothers’ identities
relations.note: Nārada reveals Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma’s identities, provoking Kamsa’s final plans.

relations.myth: Murder of Devakī’s first six sons
relations.note: Kamsa kills the six divine infants whose expanded prehistory reflects later theology.

relations.myth: Attempt to poison the infant Kṛṣṇa
relations.note: The child-killing demoness advances Kamsa’s program by offering Kṛṣṇa poisoned milk.
The whirlwind demon attacks Kṛṣṇa as an agent commonly commissioned by Kamsa.
Kamsa sends Keśin to attack Kṛṣṇa after learning his identity.
Ariṣṭa belongs to Kamsa’s asura faction, though command sequences vary.
Pralamba is affiliated with Kamsa’s demonic forces and killed by Balarāma.
Dhenuka is named among Kamsa-aligned asuras and killed by Balarāma.
Kamsa’s supernaturalized champion fights Kṛṣṇa and is killed by him.
Kamsa’s champion fights Balarāma and is killed by him.

relations.myth: Elephant ambush at the arena gate
relations.note: Kamsa stations the elephant to crush Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma before the contest.
Later lists place Bāṇa among Kamsa’s associates without securely documenting personal meetings.
Later lists place Naraka among Kamsa’s associates without securely documenting personal meetings.
